@nishant111 - reviewed `12b124b89b91f2efe6ac073eba4e73cd0b3f7642`. No high-confidence exploitable blocker found in the dependency changes, but the remediation evidence needs clarification.

The `go.mod` / `go.sum` changes are consistent: `x/crypto` moves to v0.52.0 with the required companion versions, and all eight changed module / go.mod hashes match the Go checksum database. Current CI, DCO and CLA checks are green.

1. **Please provide an authoritative reference for CVE-2026-46596, or correct the identifier.** The other six listed CVEs have upstream fixed-version evidence at v0.52.0: [GO-2026-5017](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5017.json), [GO-2026-5019](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5019.json), [GO-2026-5006](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5006.json), [GO-2026-5005](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5005.json), [GO-2026-5020](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5020.json), and [GO-2026-5021](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-5021.json). I could not corroborate CVE-2026-46596 in the public advisory sources checked; that is an evidence gap, not proof the identifier is invalid.
2. **Please include authentication regression evidence with auth tests enabled.** The existing Azure run reports success, but all seven `TestAuth_*` cases were skipped. The REST authentication path uses `x/crypto/ssh` for password authentication against fixed `127.0.0.1:22`, so the green result does not demonstrate that this runtime path was exercised.
3. **Minimum-Go compatibility remains unverified.** CI used Go 1.26.5 while `go.mod` declares 1.25.9. If that minimum is part of the supported contract, please cover it or document the intended build-toolchain requirement.

The review supports the dependency update, not a claim that every listed CVE and deployment path has been independently validated. No local Go build, `govulncheck`, live authentication exchange or DUT test was run for this review.

@StormLiangMS Thank you for the review . 
 I have addressed the validation requests and updated the CVE in the description ( apologies for the Typo in the CVE Identifier )
 
for point 2, Authentication regression validation
 
 I rebuilt commit  12b124b89b91f2efe6ac073eba4e73cd0b3f7642  and explicitly enabled the authentication tests:
 
  TOPDIR=$PWD tools/test/rest-gotest.sh \
      -bin -run Auth -authtest local,tacacs
 
 All seven top-level  TestAuth_*  cases ran and passed; none were skipped. Every GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, and DELETE subtest also passed. Valid credentials completed the actual  golang.org/x/crypto/ssh  password handshake used by  PAMAuthenAndAuthor() , while invalid users and passwords produced the expected SSH authentication failures.
 
 for point 3, Minimum-Go compatibility
 
 I repeated dependency verification and compilation with the exact minimum toolchain declared by  go.mod :
 
  go version go1.25.9 linux/amd64
 
 Using Go 1.25.9:
 
  -  go mod verify  passed.
  - The matching clean  sonic-mgmt-common  build passed.
  - Framework  make -j8 rest  passed.
  - The generated REST test binary passed the enabled authentication suite above.

Additional validation artifacts are attached as  pr170-validation-artifacts.zip .

 Authentication result excerpt:

 No  TestAuth_*  test was skipped. Every test ran its GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, and DELETE subtests. The raw log records successful  golang.org/x/crypto/ssh  password handshakes for valid credentials and the expected SSH handshake authentication failures for invalid credentials.
 
 The SSH endpoint was an isolated loopback test fixture bound to  127.0.0.1:22 . This evidence validates the framework SSH client authentication and authorization path after the dependency update; it does not claim independent validation of production PAM or TACACS infrastructure.

@yxieca Good suggestion — I'll add Go version protection similar to sonic-mgmt-common#207. Will push an update.

@yxieca Actually, looking more closely — the version protection is already in this PR! The guard checks `go.mod`'s Go version against the installed Go version and only runs `go mod tidy` when `Go >= go.mod` — exact same pattern as sonic-mgmt-common#207.

The version check block (lines 40-47 in the diff):
```makefile
@GO_MOD_VER=$$(sed -n 's/^go //p' go.mod) && \
 GO_CUR_VER=$$(\ env GOVERSION | sed 's/go//') && \
 if printf '%s\n' "$$GO_MOD_VER" "$$GO_CUR_VER" | sort -V | head -1 | grep -qx "$$GO_MOD_VER"; then \
   echo "Running go mod tidy"; \
   \ mod tidy; \
 else \
   echo "Skipping go mod tidy"; \
 fi
```

On bookworm (Go 1.21), it skips tidy. On trixie (Go 1.24), it runs tidy then vendor. Backward compatible either way.

@yxieca Thanks for the review! This PR actually already includes the same version guard as sonic-mgmt-common#207 — the `sort -V` comparison that skips `go mod tidy` when the installed Go is older than go.mod's directive. You can see it in the diff at lines 40-48 of the Makefile. Let me know if I missed something!
